transcript.answer: No, not any more. Lore's context evals did run nightly in CI for a short time. PR #2463 (merged 2026-10-02) added `.github/workflows/context-evals.yml`, which ran at 03:17 UTC every night and could also be started by hand. PR #2823 (merged 2026-10-19) removed that workflow. The evals are now experiments run from a developer machine with `scripts/context-evals/run.mjs` against the deployed lore-api, and nothing runs them on a schedule. The PR gave two reasons. The scheduled run clashed with how the evals are used, and it had gone red three nights running (10-17 to 10-19) on a single `demo-factory-todo` document that nobody read. Some documents, such as the spec for FR-9 and ADR-010, still describe a nightly job. They appear to predate the removal, and I did not check whether they were updated. I also did not find any later change that put the schedule back.

judgements.reason: The answer says no, gives the nightly run from #2463 (2026-10-02) until its removal in #2823 (2026-10-19), and says the evals now run from a developer machine, matching the gold answer.
